units.function: A deterministic in-memory planner for importing issues, comments, projects/workspaces, documents/revisions and attachments between Paperclip worktree databases. It preserves stable IDs where possible, reports drift/skips and explicitly clears missing Agent/project/goal references.
units.dependencyDirection: merge planner -> direct @paperclipai/db table inference types. The algorithm is otherwise pure, but is tightly coupled to Paperclip schema rows rather than a versioned portable transfer contract.
units.keyDataModels: WorktreeMergePlan; planned insert/skip/merge variants; import adjustments; issue/comment/document/revision/attachment/project/workspace database rows; target identity/reference sets; provisional issue/revision numbers.
units.lifecycle: Index target/source rows -> deterministically sort parents, timestamps and IDs -> classify stable-ID collisions and drift -> clear or map unavailable Agent/project/workspace/goal references -> renumber conflicting document revisions -> calculate counts/adjustments -> return a preview consumed by the imperative apply command.
units.testAssessment: The completed focused merge-history suite passed 8/8 and covers deterministic issue/comment/document/attachment planning, drift, project mapping/import and adjustment counts. It does not cover cyclic/dangling parents, unknown scope tokens, missing human identities, source/target tenant mismatch, same-ID semantic conflicts, workspace command safety, document three-way conflicts, attachment asset/object collisions, schema evolution, large inputs or property-based idempotency.
units.designRationale: Separating a pure deterministic plan from side-effectful apply makes destructive transfer explainable and testable. Stable IDs allow repeat imports to skip known records; explicit adjustment counts surface lost Agent relationships; deterministic revision renumbering avoids simple numeric collisions.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs explainable, repeatable migration/FDE template and environment promotion plans that preserve evidence provenance and responsibility while resolving identities, Connectors, data grants and executable workspace behavior explicitly.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the pure plan/apply separation, discriminated actions, deterministic ordering, stable-ID collision reporting and explicit adjustment ledger. Re-express it over Company OS versioned transfer DTOs, not database rows. Add three-way/base revisions, signed source/target snapshot digests, strict tenant and human/Agent identity mapping, responsibility/evidence dispositions, executable-field quarantine, fail-closed schema evolution and property/idempotency tests.
units.responsibilityConflict: Missing Agent attribution is silently nullified while human IDs are preserved without verifying that the same accountable principal exists in the target. Existing same-ID issues are skipped despite drift, and existing documents can be source-overwritten without an explicit conflict decision. The plan has no responsibility contract, approver, reason, evidence or data-authorization mapping.
evidence: Existing completed application:cli/__tests__/worktree-merge-history assessment reused: focused Vitest 8/8 passed
units.securityFindings: HIGH: createdBy/updatedBy/assignee user IDs are copied without confirming target-principal existence or equivalence, while missing Agent IDs are cleared; this can create dangling or falsely attributed human responsibility. HIGH: imported project workspaces carry cwd, repository, setupCommand, cleanupCommand and remote metadata without executable-field quarantine. HIGH: existing documents with matching UUID can be source-overwritten/merged without a base revision or explicit conflict policy; existing issues with drift are simply skipped, producing asymmetric silent divergence. MEDIUM: issue parent IDs are not validated against the target/import set and cycles are tolerated rather than rejected; target FK behavior becomes the accidental guard. MEDIUM: an input such as issues,unknown silently accepts issues because unknown scope tokens are discarded. MEDIUM: attachment planning checks attachment ID only, not asset ID/object-key/hash collisions. Direct database row types make future schema additions easy to omit silently. Positive properties include deterministic tie-breaks, explicit missing-reference adjustments, stable-ID deduplication, parent-first intent and isolated pure planning.
